objects: phased-in permanent with stable physical and logical identity
state_writes: one shield-counter removal through the canonical counter owner
timing: lethal-damage and deathtouch destruction execute during stabilization
targets: the bounded compiler accepts one artifact, creature, enchantment, land, permanent, artifact or enchantment, or creature or planeswalker target
resolution-time target legality is revalidated before preparation
choices: represented destination replacement choices remain owned by the canonical zone-change transaction
hidden_information: the bounded family targets only public phased-in battlefield permanents
apnap: simultaneous multiplayer destruction uses deterministic physical-object ordering before the canonical zone batch
layers: represented effective keywords determine Indestructible at preparation and commit
complete ability-changing and dependency closure remains blocked
replacement_effects: one shield counter replaces destruction caused by an effect
shield counters do not replace lethal-damage or deathtouch state-based destruction
destination replacements remain a separate canonical zone-change boundary
regeneration and competing destruction replacements remain unsupported
copy: copiable characteristics may supply Indestructible but ordinary copies do not share physical identity
control_change: a prepared transaction fails stale if the logged controller changes before commit
zone_change: a permanent is destroyed only by moving it from the battlefield to its owner's graveyard
a changed logical identity fails before mutation
source_leaves: one-shot destruction uses the resolved instruction and does not require its source to remain unless another rule says otherwise

variants: effect destruction replaced by one shield counter
closed direct-target grammar shared by spell, trigger, and activated contexts

implementation.component: typed direct-target compiler, strict destruction semantic handler, canonical destruction transaction, counter owner, and zone-transition owner

known_blockers: regeneration and effects that say a permanent cannot be regenerated are not represented
competing destruction replacement ordering beyond shield counters is incomplete
optional, modal, aggregate, quantified, relational, qualified, and compound destruction clauses remain precise compiler residuals
complete ability-changing, copy, face-down, and continuous-effect dependency interactions remain blocked
the mechanic contract is broader than the trusted bounded direct-target effect capability
